Dispersion and centroid gap along the informativeness

Source: R/plot-gap-path.R
plot_gap_path.Rd

Plots the dispersion \(H\) and the mean reliability minus \(I\) as the informativeness moves with the centered logits of the profile held fixed, as they do when only sigma_tau changes.

Usage

plot_gap_path(x, leading = TRUE, ...)

Arguments

x

An object of class reliability_profile, reliability_posterior, reliability_draws or reliability_design, or a profile_comparison of them.

leading

If TRUE (the default), dashed gray lines show the second-order terms of Proposition 2.

...

Must be empty.

Value

A patchwork object with two panels.

Details

Along the path \(dH/dm = \bar S - I\), where \(m\) is the logit of \(I\) (Lee, 2026, Proposition 2). For unequal sampling variances, \(H\) is strictly concave in \(I\) along the path and is largest at the single point where the gap crosses 0. With equal sampling variances, \(H\) and the gap are 0 throughout the path and there is no turning point. The point on each curve marks the profile's own informativeness (for a posterior fit, its posterior median), and the cross marks the turning point.

Examples

prof <- reliability_profile(se = eight_schools$se, sigma_tau = 10)
plot_gap_path(prof)
